hero.title: A mirror for your inner world
hero.subtitle: {{app_name}} helps you pause, notice patterns, and find clarity when life feels heavy. It works through reflective, emotionally attuned conversations.
hero.disclaimer: {{app_name}} is not therapy or a crisis service. If you’re in immediate danger, contact local emergency services.

howItHelps.title: How {{app_name}} Helps
howItHelps.subtitle: {{app_name}} is a gentle mirror that helps you explore feelings, recognize patterns, and reflect in a private space you control.

features.title: Reflective Conversations
features.subtitle: {{app_name}} reflects your emotions back to you, helping you name and understand what you are truly experiencing.

features.title: Spotting Patterns
features.subtitle: Over time, {{app_name}} highlights recurring themes in your thinking so you can notice connections you might have overlooked.

features.title: Private by Default

demo.title: What Makes {{app_name}} Different
demo.subtitle: See how {{app_name}} goes beyond generic advice by uncovering deeper stress triggers and offering clear, practical ways forward.

conversation.text: Hi, I can see this is a stressful moment for you. Let’s take a breath together. Can you tell me what’s weighing most heavily on you right now?
I have to close a deal with a huge client at work, and everything depends on me. I feel like if I mess up, it could ruin everything for the team… and for me.
It sounds like you’re under a lot of pressure. Maybe breaking the deal preparation into smaller steps could help reduce stress.

I hear how much responsibility is on your shoulders. There’s a **silent rule** here: you must succeed perfectly, or it’s a disaster. That belief can make your chest tighten and your thoughts race. What physical sensations are you noticing as you think about this deal?
My chest feels tight, my stomach is in knots, and I can’t focus properly. I keep imagining the worst-case scenarios.
Visualizing the worst case can increase anxiety. Focusing on actionable steps or your preparation might help you feel more in control.

That’s **catastrophizing** - imagining disasters before they happen. Recognizing this pattern is the first step. You’re preparing, and preparation is what matters. Let’s identify **one thing you can control right now**.
I guess I could review the client’s data and the proposal one more time.
Reviewing the details can help you feel more prepared. It’s a practical step to reduce uncertainty.
Exactly. That’s a **tangible step**. Focusing on what’s within your control helps quiet the mental storm. Notice that preparation is competence, not failure. How does it feel to take this small step?
A bit calmer… but I still feel like the weight of the outcome is on me alone.
Sharing responsibility or talking with a colleague might help ease that feeling. You don’t have to carry everything alone.

You’re recognizing the **pressure of carrying it alone**. What if your role was guiding the team rather than controlling everything yourself? Delegating even small tasks could lift some weight while keeping you in charge.
I could assign the financial part to Sam. I usually do it myself, but I trust him.
Delegating to a trusted team member is a practical step. It can reduce your stress while maintaining oversight.

That’s a **powerful shift** - trusting your team while staying accountable. Notice how sharing responsibility changes the tension in your body. Even small steps challenge the old rule that you must do everything perfectly.
It actually feels lighter. I didn’t expect letting go of one small part would help so much.
Even small changes in workload can have a positive effect on stress levels and performance.

Now, let’s explore what’s under the **surface pressure**. You’re worried about judgment and failing your team. That’s a lot of **internal pressure**. What’s the story you tell yourself when you imagine failing?
I keep thinking I’ll look incompetent, that people will doubt me, and maybe I’ll lose respect. It feels humiliating even imagining it.
Fears of judgment are common. It might help to reframe failure as a learning opportunity rather than a reflection of your worth.

I hear the **fear of being judged**. That’s a strong core belief influencing your stress. You’re not your mistakes - you’re a competent professional facing a challenge. If you notice this fear without acting on it, how does it shift in your body?
It’s still tense, but less like panic… more like awareness.

Exactly. That’s the difference between **reactive overwhelm** and **conscious awareness**. You can feel the fear without letting it control your actions. Let’s try naming one positive aspect about your preparation or skills.
I’ve been thorough with my research and proposals. I know the client’s needs well.
Recognizing your preparedness helps build confidence. Focus on your strengths to counteract anxiety.
Perfect. That’s **anchoring in competence**. Every time your mind jumps to worst-case scenarios, you can return to this grounded fact: you are prepared and capable. How does that feel?
It makes me feel a little steadier, more in control.

Now, let’s consider **what asking for support might look like**. It doesn’t mean weakness - it’s a strength. Even asking one team member for input or feedback can reduce pressure. Who could you approach safely for insight?
Maybe I can ask Sarah to review the proposal. She’s detail-oriented, and I trust her judgment.
Getting feedback from someone trustworthy is a concrete way to ease stress and catch potential issues.

Exactly. That’s **strategic collaboration**. You’re not giving up control - you’re amplifying effectiveness while reducing internal pressure. Notice how even thinking about sharing feels in your body and mind.
It feels relieving… like the weight in my chest has lessened a bit.
Sharing tasks and responsibilities can reduce emotional load and help maintain focus.

Before we close, let’s integrate today’s insights. You practiced **preparation, delegation, emotional awareness, and collaboration**. You challenged the old rule that you must carry everything alone and perfectly. Notice the shift: your strength isn’t in perfection, but in conscious, deliberate action.
I really feel that. I’m calmer and more confident, and I know I’m not alone in handling this.
Recognizing your progress and building on it will help maintain confidence and reduce stress over time.

You did something significant today. You acknowledged your fear, noticed your body, challenged old rules, and practiced self-compassion. That’s real strength. You can take this into the meeting tomorrow with clarity and grounded focus. You’re ready.

generic.title: Generic AI Approach
points: Gives **one-size-fits-all tips** without really tuning into you
Overlooks the **emotional undercurrents** behind your words
Doesn't notice when your thoughts turn **harsh or unrealistic**
Misses chances to offer **deeper understanding or relief**

app.title: {{app_name}}'s Difference
points: Notices when your thoughts make situations feel **bigger or scarier** than they really are
Helps you spot **black and white thinking** that leaves no room for balance
Uncovers hidden rules you’ve been living by, like *always needing to be available*
Gives you **practical ways** to shift your thoughts so they feel lighter and less rigid

earlyAccess.title: Be Among {{app_name}}’s First Users
earlyAccess.subtitle: We are inviting a select group of women to join {{app_name}}’s tester program. Share your experiences and needs to help us fine-tune {{app_name}} so it truly sees, hears, and understands you.

items.question: What is {{app_name}}?
items.answer: {{app_name}} is an emotional mirror. It helps you slow down, reflect, and see your inner world with more clarity through short, emotionally attuned conversations.

items.question: How is {{app_name}} different from therapy?
items.answer: {{app_name}} is not therapy and cannot replace professional care. It is a daily reflective companion designed to support awareness, not to diagnose or treat mental health conditions.

items.question: How does {{app_name}} actually work?
items.answer: {{app_name}} uses carefully designed prompts and conversational patterns to reflect emotions back to you. It highlights hidden pressures, recurring thoughts, and unspoken rules so you can better understand yourself.

items.question: Is my data private?
items.answer: Yes. Your reflections belong to you. Conversations are private by design, and you will have the ability to export or delete your data.

items.question: Who is {{app_name}} for?
items.answer: {{app_name}} is built for people who carry a lot, often appear strong on the outside, but feel emotionally drained inside. It offers them a safe space to reflect, recognize patterns, and reclaim clarity.

items.question: Can {{app_name}} help in a crisis?
items.answer: No. {{app_name}} is not a crisis service. If you are in immediate danger or facing a mental health emergency, please contact local emergency services or a professional hotline.

items.question: How much does it cost?
items.answer: During early access, {{app_name}} is free to use. Pricing will be introduced later as we grow with feedback from early users.

items.question: Why should I join early access?
items.answer: Early access lets you shape {{app_name}} with us. Your feedback will directly influence how the experience evolves, and you will be among the first to benefit from new features.

disclaimer.label: Important:
disclaimer.message: {{app_name}} is not a mental health or crisis service. If you are experiencing a crisis, please reach out to your local emergency services immediately
